{{Short description|Canadian physicist (1937–2019)}}
'''Varley Fullerton Sears''' (born 1937, died at age 81 in [[Deep River, Ontario]] on June 9, 2019<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.valleyfuneralhome.ca/obits/obituary.php?id=675783 |title = Dr. Varley Sears Obituary - Valley Funeral Home}}</ref>) was a Canadian physicist, notable for his contributions to the methodological foundations of [[neutron scattering]].

In 1960, Sears obtained a Ph.D. from the [[University of Toronto]] with a thesis on ''The rotational absorption spectrum of solid and liquid parahydrogen''.<ref>{{Cite thesis|url = http://search.library.utoronto.ca/details?3468410|title = The rotational absorption spectrum of solid and liquid parahydrogen|year = 1960|archive-date = 2014-11-13|access-date = 2014-11-13|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20141113184113/http://search.library.utoronto.ca/details?3468410|url-status = dead}}</ref> From 1963 to 1965, the [[National Research Council of Canada]] sent him as an ''Overseas Postdoctoral Fellow'' to the [[Clarendon Laboratory]] in Oxford where he was hosted by [[Roger James Elliott]] and worked on [[Raman scattering]] by semiconductors.<ref>{{cite journal | doi = 10.1088/0370-1328/84/6/314 | volume=84 | issue=6 | title=Theory of the Schottky anomaly for strong spin-lattice coupling | year=1964 | journal=Proceedings of the Physical Society | pages=951–967 | last1 = Sears | first1 = V F| bibcode=1964PPS....84..951S }}</ref> Back in Canada, he became a staff scientist in the ''Theoretical Physics Branch'' of [[Chalk River Laboratories]]. In 1966/67, he published seminal papers on neutron spectra of molecular rotors.<ref>VF Sears Can. J. Phys. 44, 1279 (1966), ibid 44, 1299 (1966), ibid 45, 237 (1967).</ref> By the 1980s, he had become a leading expert in [[neutron optics]], publishing a review<ref>{{cite journal | doi = 10.1016/0370-1573(82)90151-X | volume=82 | issue=1 | title=Fundamental aspects of neutron optics | year=1982 | journal=Physics Reports | pages=1–29 | last1 = Sears | first1 = V.F.| bibcode=1982PhR....82....1S }}</ref> and a textbook<ref>VF Sears 1989: ''Neutron optics: an introduction to the theory of neutron optical phenomena and their applications'' - Oxford University Press. Review by [[Anton Zeilinger]] at http://scitation.aip.org/content/aip/magazine/physicstoday/article/43/7/10.1063/1.2810631.</ref> on the subject. Based on these foundations, he compiled authoritative tables of [[neutron scattering length]]s.<ref>[https://inis.iaea.org/search/search.aspx?orig_q=RN:17034467 VF Sears 1984, ''Thermal-neutron scattering lengths and cross sections for condensed-matter research''] - Atomic Energy of Canada Ltd., Chalk River, Ontario. Chalk River Nuclear Labs.</ref><ref>VF Sears 1986, ''Neutron Scattering Lengths and Cross Sections'' in Methods in Experimental Physics Volume 23A, pp 521–550.</ref><ref>{{cite journal | doi = 10.1080/10448639208218770 | volume=3 | issue=3 | title=Neutron scattering lengths and cross sections | year=1992 | journal=Neutron News | pages=26–37 | last1 = Sears | first1 = Varley F.}}</ref> In 1997, he published a generic solution of the [[Darwin-Hamilton equations]] that provide an approximative description of multiple Bragg reflection by a [[mosaic crystal]].<ref>VF Sears 1997 ''Acta Crystallogr'' A53, 35-45.</ref>

He was elected a [[Fellow of the American Physical Society]] in 1990. <ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=1990&unit_id=&institution=|title=APS Fellow Archive|publisher=APS|accessdate= 7 October 2020}} </ref>
